My story

I WAS
TOLD I
WAS
WORTH
NOTHING.

"If you burp, it means the poison is leaving. You have a warm strong sun inside — rely on it, follow it, allow it to guide you."

The sentence I needed three years ago.

The chapters

Chapter 01

The Beginning

I grew up in Kyiv being told I was worth nothing. My mother's voice. My father — a psychologist — was my counterweight, guide, and north star. Early on I learned to read a room fast, to detect danger in a face before it arrived. That hypervigilance never left me. It became a skill.

Chapter 02

The Champion

I became downhill cycling champion of Ukraine. No family support, no sponsor — just obsession and speed. I know what it takes to build an identity from zero. I also know what it feels like when someone destroys it. A boyfriend stole my bike and sold it. I couldn't compete. That loss taught me more about resilience than any victory.

Chapter 03

The Escape

I taught myself to code and got hired in Berlin and Zurich — no degree, pure obsession. Then Zurich became a cage. I was living my husband's life: his mountains, his adrenaline, his rules. When war started in Ukraine he found someone else. On crutches, I left.

Chapter 04

The Dark Room

Three years of fighting — in courts and inside myself. I didn't know who I was. Document dependencies kept me tied to a marriage I'd already left. One night I asked a friend to tattoo my arms until dawn. I needed the inner pain to have a physical form. Now those marks are mine.

Chapter 05

The Rebuild

Moutier. French lessons. Books. Real work on myself. I found something rarer than talent: self-love built from the ground up, alone, after everything. I stopped doing work I hated for people who didn't value it. I stopped betraying myself. Now I help others do the same.

Now

Why This Work

I spent years being excellent at things nobody could see. Not because I wasn't showing up — because I didn't know what I looked like from the outside. No one was honest enough to tell me. That gap is exactly what I now close for the people I work with. I'm not a strategist who studied this in a classroom. I lived it. My eye for this comes from being on both sides of the same invisible wall.

What I actually do
